_about: 2028 seat model v2.3 (.build/analysis/seat-model/swing-simulate.mjs), mode nowcast: 20,000 simulated elections. Logit swing from 2025 with seat terms fitted on 1996-2025 (sitting members - who sits now, by-elections, defections and retirements since 2025 included - and reversion of each seat's 2025 surprise); independents drawn from the record (a sitting independent on sitting independents' own drift and spread; one challenge in every seat a party holds, its share drawn from what happened next in seats whose independent had polled about the same at the last three elections); preferences replayed on each division's 2025 Senate rankings (House-calibrated; the Coalition's Labor-v-One Nation and One Nation's Labor-v-Coalition levels set to the site's flow tables), an independent's take of them by who else is left in the count; fitted polling, state, seat-type, education, seat and flow errors. Nowcast: an election held now, final-month polling error, no fade. HARD LIMITS: no one is nominated - the parties' 2025 field is assumed and no independent challenger is a named person; the 2025 boundaries are used (Tasmania, South Australia and the ACT have since been redrawn); how-to-vote decisions are not modelled beyond the 2025 Senate-to-House offsets (a Coalition card putting Labor above One Nation would move many seats); intervals are floor, not ceiling.

national.headline: Labor would probably win the most seats, probably short of a majority
